explanation: The Almighty Creator who sends the prophet Jonah with a message of repentance to the people of Nineveh.
The prophet who reluctantly obeys God's call and travels to the great city to proclaim judgment over its sinfulness.
The capital of the Assyrian Empire, described as a large city that took three days to walk across from one end to the other.
The act by which the people, from king to commoner, turn back to God through fasting and wearing sackcloth to show their humility.
Coarse woolen fabric used as a sign of mourning, repentance, and prayer in ancient Israel and surrounding regions.
To abstain from food and drink as part of a religious practice to express serious remorse and seek God's mercy.
God's compassion in choosing not to destroy Nineveh because the people showed genuine repentance.
